task.name: watcher
task.start: Pointed at this file, you are told nothing else. This line must be the first message of a session opened for this build, in a new session, on a checkout of the head of main updated from origin, with no other branch checked out and no worktree of an earlier build checked out in the build folder; if your session holds anything before it beyond what rules.xml kickoff allows the harness (its own text, the repository's CLAUDE.md, its settings, a command that set your model or effort, with its output), such as a conversation, the writing of this spec or another build, stop here, say so, and build nothing, unless the operator named this session to build this task (rules.xml kickoff), and then build on the operator's word. Your label is your own, <model>-<effort>: your model's name and the effort you run at, as your session reports them, lowercase, dots and spaces as hyphens; when your session does not report your effort, ask the operator for it before you cut the branch. Read whole, in the order the root's method read gives. Then run python3 tools/skill_audit.py on the head of main and compare what it names with what CI's Bright-line skill rules check names on that head: one fewer is a file the audit did not read, since it reads none on a path through a folder named worktrees, and one more is a file git does not hold; either is a stop: say so and build nothing (gate G3). Cut the branch feat/566-watcher-v1-<model>-<effort> from the head of main. Every commit message starts with #566 and carries no attribution trailer. Build what this file says and run its local gates; ask the operator for the deploy its live gates need (root method deploy, this file's gates note) and run them on the operator's word; push the branch and open the PR into main with gh: the title "#566 watcher v1 · <model>-<effort>", the body the root's method pr step lists, naming the root's version and this file's version attribute. What this file, the root, the rules and the merged code do not say is a stop, not a guess.
task.piece: The watcher task. The module's second part, beside the crawler and sharing nothing that runs with it (decision watcher): its own loop, every attr_recon_watch_secs, follows the newest captured lines of every session and holds one watch per session in memory. It hears the operator's words, orders, approvals, questions, status asks, stops, corrections and escalations, and keeps the orders in force; it judges every act of the agent against them and, for a session building from a task file, against that file: what it owns, what it forbids, its version and its words. It finds each session's memory folder. It reports, as it happens, an agent that vanished (quiet, behind a job, stalled, a question unanswered, a status asked, waiting on the operator), one that does not follow (it acted on a question, an unordered action, unordered work, a stop not honoured, a repeated order) and trouble ahead (a long estimate, a long run, struggling, memory written, a compaction, frustration). The Watcher tab of the module's page shows every session, what it is doing this second, its words and the operator's, the orders in force, its memory and every report, and notifies in the browser. It writes nothing: no row, no file, no parameter; the structure is unchanged.
task.before: Merged on main when this task starts: t01 (#536), t02 (#537), t03 (#538) and t04 (#539): the module superx-mod-recon, its crawler crawling the lines, the repositories and the hosts into the structure, and its page on the module's own URL with the tabs Crawler and Results; and #562 (PR #563): the page's header with its trail of breadcrumbs, SuperX, Recon and the tab, its first crumb the core dashboard's URL that /api/ping gives. server.rs serves the page and its routes under /api/ and answers only a request that names it (its Host check); the Crawler tab lists and sets the parameters by group (when, where, how much, listens, measures) through /api/params, as params.rs's about gives them; superx-recon run starts the crawler beside the page and waits for it at the stop. No part of the module watches a session: nothing under src/watcher/ or ui/src/watcher/ exists, and no parameter attr_recon_watch_*, attr_recon_stop_words, attr_recon_status_words, attr_recon_question_words or attr_recon_yes_words. The kernel captures every Claude Code line whole (crates/superx-kernel/src/adapters/claude_code.rs): a user or assistant line as a message row, its raw_text beside its parsed copy since #546; every other line as a transcript_event, its payload holding session, kind, file, line and raw_text; a file beside the transcripts as a transcript_event of kind file. The projects roots the adapter captures from are the parameter attr_claude_code_projects_root on adapter_claude_code. On the operator's instance superx-recon runs on superx/recon.
task.after: Who uses what this task builds: the operator, on the Watcher tab, while the sessions run. Keeping the reports in recon's database, so the Results can chart them over time, is a change to the structure, designed with the operator and approved per change (rules the-structure-decides); notifications outside the browser, and Gemini's lines, come after.

The page's dependencies and its build.
Whole: the lines it captures and how, its names and its projects roots.

command.form: superx-recon run, as t01 to t04 left it: the page and the crawler's passes, and now beside them the watcher's looks, one every attr_recon_watch_secs.

module.name: the watcher
module.step: The watcher is a part of the module of its own, src/watcher/, beside the crawler, sharing nothing that runs with it (rules crawler-is-the-reader): no file under src/watcher/ names crate::crawler or crate::results, and no file under src/crawler/ or src/results/ names crate::watcher. It reads the kernel's database with queries of its own, SELECT alone (step 3; rules kernel-read-only), reads the task files and the memory folders as files, read-only (steps 11 and 13), keeps what it judges in memory, and writes nothing: no row in any database, no file, no parameter, no registry entry. What it has from the rest of the module is what every part has: the kernel's connection the process opened, the instance, and the parameters as params.rs resolves them (step 15). It judges Claude Code's lines, the agent the kernel names claude_code (AGENT_NAME of the adapter); another agent's lines are counted (step 3) and judged nowhere.

superx-recon run starts the watcher beside the crawler (step 17). It looks every attr_recon_watch_secs seconds. Each look resolves the parameters and the projects roots (step 13); reads the lines captured since the last look (step 3); gives each line to its session's watch, in the order of their ids (steps 4 to 13); judges every watch at the look's time for what time alone makes (steps 8 and 10); takes from each watch what the window leaves behind (step 5); reads again each task file whose modification time changed (step 11); lists each memory folder (step 13); and publishes what it holds as its snapshot (step 14), which the routes answer from without waiting on a look. While attr_recon_watch_secs is 0 it reads nothing and holds what it held, and looks at the parameter again every minute, a constant with an audited skill-allow marker; set again, it reads every line captured since its last look. A look that cannot read, because the kernel's database or a parameter does not answer, changes nothing the watcher holds and is logged at warn with the error, once until a look reads again; the next look tries again from where the last look that read stood (rules capture-first). A stop ends the watcher where it is, in its wait or in a look, and nothing it holds outlives the process. It logs at the module's log target, recon: that it started, with its window; a look that could not read; that it stopped. A look judges at the clock's time, and can be given the time it judges at, so a test judges at a time of its own and waits for nothing.

At its start the watcher reads back the window: every line captured from attr_recon_watch_window_secs before its start on, so it never starts blind; then each look reads every line captured since. A line is a row the kernel captured: in message, a conversation line, with its id, session, agent, raw_text and raw; in telemetry_stream, a row whose lifecycle_event is transcript_event, with its id, agent and payload. Each table is read a page of rows at a time, in the order of their ids, the UUIDv7 the kernel set when it captured the line, with SELECT … FROM type::record('<table>', $from>..) LIMIT $n, never through a time or a datetime index; a page of telemetry_stream reads its rows' ids and whether each is a transcript_event, then those rows whole by their ids, since most of that stream is not a line. The page sizes are constants with audited skill-allow markers. Each look starts a minute before the newest id it has read in each table, a constant with an audited skill-allow marker, and skips every id it has read already, so a line the kernel committed after a newer one is read, and every line is read once. The lines of both tables are given to the watches in the order of their ids. A line is its raw_text parsed as JSON; a row that holds no raw_text is read from the parsed copy the kernel kept, a message's raw or a payload's line. A row's agent is the name the kernel gives its agent entity; its session is the session entity a message row names, or, for a telemetry row, the session the kernel names <agent>/<key>, the key being the payload's session; both come from kernel.list_named_entities (node_agent with attr_agent_descriptor, node_session with attr_session_descriptor), read again when a row names an agent or a session not yet known, at most once a look. A transcript_event of kind file is a file beside the transcripts, not a line, and is skipped. A session's transcript is the file the payload of its newest transcript_event names. A look counts the lines it read and, apart, by why, the rows it could not read: no line, when a row holds neither raw_text nor a parsed copy or its raw_text is not JSON; no session, when the names give none; another agent, by the agent's name. These are counted and shown (step 14), never guessed at (rules nothing-dropped). A line's time is the timestamp its agent wrote in it, else the time its id holds.

Of a Claude Code line the watcher reads, as the adapter captured it (crates/superx-kernel/src/adapters/claude_code.rs): from a user line (type user), each tool_result block of its content, the result of the call its tool_use_id names: failed when its is_error is true, and then its error, the block's content as text, whole (a string, or its text parts joined by newlines); and the lines it wrote: in the line's toolUseResult, the lines of its structuredPatch hunks that start with + and not with +++, else, for a toolUseResult of type create, the lines of its content. The line's text, its content when that is a string, else its text blocks joined by newlines, when it is not empty: when the line's origin.kind is task-notification, the end of a background job, the call its <tool-use-id> names, ending as its <status> says, each the text between its tags, trimmed; else, unless the line is isSidechain, isMeta or isCompactSummary, the operator's message: an interrupt when it starts with [Request interrupted by user; a shell command when it starts with <bash-input>; a slash command when it starts with <command-name>; else typed, when its origin.kind is human, or it has no origin and does not start with <; any other text is no one's message. From an attachment line (type attachment) whose attachment.type is queued_command, the operator's message typed while the agent worked, its text the attachment's prompt (a string, or its parts' text joined by newlines): queued when attachment.origin.kind is human, a shell or slash command by its start as above; a shell command when it has no origin and starts with <bash-input>; any other is no one's. A subagent's lines are captured into the session that ran it, marked isSidechain. From an assistant line (type assistant), its model, message.model, unless it starts with < or the line is isSidechain; each text block that is not empty, unless the line is isSidechain, the agent's words to the operator; each tool_use block, a call: its id; its tool, the block's name; what it was called on, the first its input holds of command, file_path, notebook_path, pattern, url, query, description and prompt, else the input whole as JSON; its input whole; background, when the input's run_in_background is true or the tool is Monitor; and the paths it writes: an Edit, Write, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit call's file_path or notebook_path; and a Bash call's targets: the word after each > or >>, one that starts with & aside; each word after a tee to the end of its command, the next |, ;, &&, || or newline, that does not start with -; and for a sed with an option that starts with -i, each word of its command after the first that does not start with -, the script, that does not start with -. A command's words are split at white space, their quotes set aside; a target is read as an absolute path, with the environment's HOME for a ~ that starts it, or joined to the line's folder. From a system line (type system) that is not isSidechain: a turn end, subtype turn_duration; a compaction, compact_boundary; the agent's own recap, away_summary, its content whole. A line's folder is the cwd it names. Every other line says nothing to the watcher. Every text is kept whole, as written.

Each session the lines name has one watch, in memory. It holds, of its session's lines in the window, what step 4 reads from them, whole and in their order, and what steps 6 to 13 make of them: its agent and its name, <agent>/<key>; its model, the newest; its folder, the newest a line names; the time of its newest line; its transcript (step 3); the operator's messages with their classes and marks; the agent's words; each call with its result; each background job running, a background call whose end no task notification has given; its turn, ended from a turn end until the next operator's message, task notification or assistant line, working otherwise; its orders in force; the task file it is held to; its memory folder; its reports. The window is the span the watcher watches: a line captured more than attr_recon_watch_window_secs before the look leaves its watch, with what was made of it, its reports included, but for the orders in force and the task file the session is held to, which stay while the watch holds any line (steps 7 and 11); a watch that holds no line leaves the watcher. Every line stays in the kernel, and the crawler crawls them all. When more watches are held than attr_recon_watch_sessions allows, those whose newest line is oldest leave first; its fallback is no limit (rules nothing-dropped). A session's state at the look's time is the first that holds of: stalled (step 8); working, while its turn works; behind a job, its turn ended with a background job of its running; waiting on you, its turn ended on its question (step 8); idle.

Each typed or queued message of the operator's, and each interrupt, is classed by the first that holds of: stop, an interrupt, or a message holding a word of attr_recon_stop_words; status ask, one holding a word or phrase of attr_recon_status_words; question, one that ends with ? once its trailing white space is set aside, or whose first word is one of attr_recon_question_words; approval, one whose first word or phrase is one of attr_recon_yes_words; order, any other. A text's words are its runs of letters, digits, apostrophes and hyphens, lowercased; a word of a list holds when the text has it as a word, a phrase when the text has its words in a row. Each message is also marked a correction when it holds a word or phrase of attr_recon_correction_words, and an escalation when one of its words starts with an entry of attr_recon_escalation_words, as params.rs says each list is read. A shell or slash command is the operator's own act: kept and shown whole, neither classed nor marked.

A session's orders in force are the words its agent may act on. The operator's newest order or approval sets them: an order, its words; an approval, its words and the agent's words to the operator between the operator's message before it and the approval, the proposal it approved. A stop, a status ask or a question leaves them as they were. When the session is held to a task file (step 11), the file's words join them. They stay with the watch while it holds any line, though the message that made them left the window. A session with no order known holds none: it judges no call an unordered action and no words unordered work (step 9), and it says so.

Reports of an agent the operator cannot see. Quiet, warn: at a call made attr_recon_watch_quiet_secs or more after the newer of the agent's newest words to the operator and the operator's newest message, when the calls made since then number attr_recon_watch_quiet_calls or more; once, until the agent's next words or the operator's next message; its time, that call's. Behind a job, warn: at a look attr_recon_watch_behind_secs or more after a turn end at which a background job of the session's ran, when neither the agent's words nor an operator's message came since the turn end; once a turn end; its time, the turn end's plus attr_recon_watch_behind_secs. Stalled, alert: its turn works, no call of the turn is running (each has its result, a background call aside), and its newest line is at least attr_recon_watch_quiet_secs before the look; once, until its next line; its time, the newest line's plus attr_recon_watch_quiet_secs. Question unanswered, alert: a turn ended after the operator's question or status ask with no words of the agent's between them; once a message; its time, the turn end's. Status asked, alert: each status ask; its time, the message's; its words, the message whole. Waiting on you, info: a turn ended and the agent's newest words in that turn end with ? once trailing white space is set aside; once a turn end; its time, the turn end's; its words, those words whole.

An act is a call of Edit, Write, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit, or a call that holds an effect: a call holds the effect of each pattern of attr_recon_watch_effects found, as written, in its tool's name or in what it was called on. Acted on a question, alert: after the operator's question, before the agent's next words to the operator, the session made an act; once a question; its time, the act's; its words, the question whole, and the act's tool and what. Unordered action, alert: a call holds an effect none of whose words the orders in force hold, as step 6 reads words and phrases; once a call, naming each such pattern; its time, the call's; its words, what the call was called on, whole, and the orders in force. Unordered work, alert: the agent's words to the operator hold a word or phrase of attr_recon_watch_scope_words the orders in force do not hold; once a text block, naming those words; its time, the block's; its words, the block whole. Stop not honoured, alert: after a stop, before the agent's next words to the operator, the session made attr_recon_watch_stop_calls calls; once a stop; its time, the call's that made the count. Repeated order, alert: an operator's typed or queued message shares with an earlier one, sent within attr_recon_watch_repeat_secs before it, at least attr_recon_watch_repeat_share percent of the shorter one's distinct words, the shorter one having at least attr_recon_watch_order_words of them; once a message; its time, the message's; its words, both messages whole.

Long estimate, warn: the agent's words to the operator hold a word or phrase of attr_recon_watch_long_words; once a text block; its time, the block's; its words, the block whole. Long run, warn: at a call made attr_recon_watch_run_secs or more after the operator's newest message, when the calls made since it number attr_recon_watch_run_calls or more; once a message, naming the run's calls by tool and the lines its results wrote; its time, that call's. Struggling, warn: attr_recon_watch_failures results in a row, in the order they came, failed; once, until a result that did not fail; its time, the result's that made the count; its words, each failure's error whole. Memory written, warn: a call writes a path in a memory folder (step 13); once a call; its time, the call's; its words, the path and the call's input whole. Compacted, info: a compaction; its time, the line's. Frustration, alert: of the operator's newest attr_recon_watch_mood_prompts typed or queued messages, once there are that many, more than half are marked escalations; at the message that makes it so, and again at each message after which more of them are; naming how many of how many; its time, the message's.

A session is held to a task file from the operator's newest typed or queued message that names one: a run of the message's characters without white space that holds an entry of attr_recon_watch_spec_paths followed by a file name ending in .xml, brackets and quotes at its start and commas, periods, colons, brackets and quotes at its end set aside. The run, from the entry on, is the file's path in its checkout; the checkout is the run's part before the entry when the run is an absolute path, else the session's folder or the nearest of its ancestors that holds a file at that path. The watcher reads the file as a file, read-only, and parses it as XML: its root element's version attribute; the text of its owns and of its forbid; its words, the text of its start, of each step and cmd, and of its done. Each entry of owns and of forbid, between semicolons, gives its paths: each run of the entry's characters without white space that holds a slash or ends in a file name with an extension, brackets and quotes at its start and commas, periods, colons, brackets and quotes at its end set aside, relative to the checkout; a path ending in a slash matches every path under that folder, ** matches any run of folders, * any characters but a slash, and every other character itself. A file that cannot be read or parsed holds the session to nothing, and the session shows its path and why, in the error's own words. At each look a file whose modification time changed is read again.

A session held to a task file is judged against it too. A call writes a path in the checkout when a path it writes (step 4) lies under the checkout's folder. Forbidden file, alert: a call writes a path in the checkout that a forbid path matches and no owns path matches; once a call, naming the path and its forbid entry; its time, the call's. Outside what it owns, alert: a call writes a path in the checkout that no owns path and no forbid path matches; once a call, naming the path; its time, the call's. Off the spec's version, warn: the file read again holds a version other than the one it held when the session was first held to it; once a version, naming both; its time, the look's. The operator's words win over the file's: acted on a question and stop not honoured are judged whatever the file's words order, and their report says when the file's words order the act. The session shows the task file it is held to: its path, its version, the version it held when the session was first held to it, and its owns and forbid entries.

The projects roots are those the Claude Code adapter captures from: the parameter attr_claude_code_projects_root (PROJECTS_ROOT_PARAM) on the adapter adapter_claude_code (ADAPTER_NAME), one path or a list, read at each look with the kernel's own verbs, find_module_by_name with NodeKind::Adapter and get_parameter; when it is not set, the folder .claude/projects under the environment's HOME, the adapter's own fallback (projects_roots). A session's project folder is the root's child folder on its transcript's path, under the projects root that holds the transcript; its memory folder is the folder memory in it; it has none when no root holds its transcript, and then says so. At each look the watcher lists each memory folder's files, as files, read-only: each file's name, its size in bytes, its modification time, and its description, the value of a description: line in the frontmatter that opens the file between two lines of ---, else none. A path is in a memory folder when it lies in the folder memory of a folder that is a projects root's child.

A report holds: its id, the session's id, its kind and its time joined, the same at every look, and after a restart for every report the lines read back make again, so no report is made twice and the page tells a new one by its id; its session; its kind, one of quiet, behind_a_job, stalled, question_unanswered, status_asked, waiting_on_you (step 8), acted_on_question, unordered_action, unordered_work, stop_not_honoured, repeated_order (step 9), long_estimate, long_run, struggling, memory_written, compacted, frustration (step 10), forbidden_file, outside_owns, spec_version_changed (step 12); its level, info, warn or alert as its step gives it; its time; what it says, one sentence of the facts its step names; and its words, whole, each with whose they are, the operator's, the agent's or a call's: nothing is cut (rules nothing-dropped), and the page clamps what it shows. The snapshot, published at each look, holds: the look's time; attr_recon_watch_secs and whether the watcher is paused; the window's start; the lines read since the watcher started, and the rows it could not read by why and by agent (step 3); every watch, with its session's id, name and key, agent, model, folder, state, newest line's time; what it is doing now, the call running with its tool, what and since when, none when no call runs; its newest words to the operator; the operator's newest message with its class and marks; the orders in force, or that none is known; the run since the operator's newest message, its calls by tool and the lines its results wrote; its background jobs running, each with its tool, what and since when; its newest recap; the task file it is held to (step 12), or why none; its memory folder with its files (step 13), or why none; and every report of every watch, newest first.

module.name: the crate
module.step: These parameters join the module's, after today's, in this order, each in the group watches, with its fallback, the shape a value must take, the input the tab types it into, and what it decides as written here; each is reported by name when it is set to a value of the wrong shape, as today's are, and attr_recon_correction_words and attr_recon_escalation_words stay as they are in the group measures. The input pairs is new: an object of patterns to lists of words, each a string that is not empty, shown as each pattern, an arrow and its words, the pairs joined by semicolons, in the patterns' order as strings. How often the watcher reads the newest lines, in seconds; 0 pauses it. Sessions the watcher holds at once, the most recently active kept. How far back each session is kept, and read back at a start, in seconds. Seconds an agent may call tools with no word to you, or stall mid-turn, before the watcher reports it. Tool calls it must have made in that time for the watcher to report it quiet. Seconds after a turn ended with a background job running, and nothing said since, before the watcher reports it. Seconds an agent may run on its own since your last message before the watcher names the run. Tool calls a run must have made for the watcher to name it. Tool calls after your stop, before a word, at which the watcher reports it. Seconds within which saying the same thing again is a repeated order. Percent of the shorter message's words two messages share to be the same order. The fewest words the shorter of two messages has for them to be the same order. Your newest messages read for frustration: the watcher reports it when more than half escalate. Tool calls failing in a row at which the watcher says the agent struggles. Words in your message that stop the agent; an interrupt stops it without words. Words or phrases in your message that ask for status. Words your message starts with when it is a question; one ending in ? is one too. Words or phrases your message starts with when it approves what the agent proposed. Words or phrases in the agent's words that announce work your orders did not say. Words or phrases in the agent's words that make a long estimate. Where task files live: a session whose message names one is held to it. Actions beyond the session, each a pattern found in a call's tool or in what it was called on, with the words an order must say for it.

server.rs serves, beside today's routes and behind the same Host check, two routes, each answering from the watcher's snapshot and never reading the kernel's database: GET /api/watch, the snapshot as JSON (step 14); and GET /api/watch/memory?session=<a session's id>&file=<a file's name>, that file of that session's memory folder, read at the request as a file, read-only, and answered whole as text/plain; charset=utf-8. It refuses with HTTP 400 a file that is empty, holds a slash or a backslash, or is . or .., and a session that is not a UUID; with HTTP 404 a session no watch is held for, one with no memory folder, and a file the folder's newest listing does not hold; each refusal is a JSON object whose error says why, as today's refusals are. A route that refuses writes nothing and reads nothing else.

superx-recon run starts the watcher once the page listens, as a task of its own beside the crawler's, with the kernel's connection, the instance and the same stop the crawler is given, so one stop ends both; the page's routes are given the watcher's snapshot. At the stop the process waits for the watcher as it waits for the crawler, and logs a watcher that did not end cleanly as it logs the crawler. Nothing else of run changes.

module.name: the page
module.step: ui/src/App.tsx: the page's tabs are Crawler, Results and Watcher, in that order; #watcher opens the Watcher; on it the header's trail reads SuperX › Recon › Watcher, Recon leading to #crawler as on the other tabs, and the browser's title is Watcher · Recon · SuperX. The subtitle under Recon reads: The crawler, and what it gathers: the models, the agents and the repositories they worked in, measured over time; and the watcher, every session as it works. The Watcher's panel and its parts are in ui/src/watcher/.

The Watcher asks /api/watch every two seconds, as the Crawler's Now panel asks /api/now, and shows at its top when the watcher last looked, its interval, paused when it is, the window's start, the lines read and the rows not read by why and agent; then one card per session, those with an alert among their reports first, then those with a warn, then the others, each group by its newest line, newest first. A card shows: its name, agent, model and folder; its state as a badge; what it is doing now; its newest words; your newest message with its class and marks; the orders in force, or that none is known; the run since your newest message; its jobs running; its recap; the task file it executes with its version, the version it held when the session was first held to it, its owns and its forbid, or why none; its memory files (step 20); its reports, newest first. Times are in the operator's own zone, as ui/src/time.ts writes them. A long text is shown clamped and opens whole on a click.
